column1: 1:1|Paul, an apostle of Christ Jesus by God's will, and Timothy our brother,|Retains Paul's commissioned role, divine agency and Timothy's family designation.

1:2|to the saints and faithful brothers and sisters in Christ at Colossae: Grace and peace to you from God our Father.|Keeps the location, paired community descriptions and the pinned source's short blessing.
1:3|We always thank God, the Father of our Lord Jesus Christ, when we pray for you,|Preserves the repeated thanksgiving and names its addressee and occasion.
1:4|because we have heard of your faith in Christ Jesus and the love you have for all the saints,|Keeps faith's object and love's comprehensive human direction.

1:5|because of the hope stored up for you in heaven. You heard about this hope beforehand in the word of truth, the good news|Preserves hope as the ground and retains both word-of-truth and good-news descriptions.

1:6|that has come to you. Just as it is bearing fruit and growing throughout the whole world, so it has among you since the day you heard it and truly understood God's grace.|Keeps the paired growth images, worldwide scope and the local beginning.
1:7|You learned it from Epaphras, our beloved fellow slave, who is a faithful minister of Christ on our behalf.|Retains Epaphras's name, slave language and representative service.
1:8|He also told us about your love in the Spirit.|Keeps the report and its spiritual setting without expanding the relation.

1:9|For this reason, from the day we heard, we have not stopped praying for you and asking that you be filled with the knowledge of his will in all spiritual wisdom and understanding,|Preserves the unceasing prayer, filling image and full pair of cognitive gifts.

1:10|so that you may walk worthy of the Lord and please him in every way: bearing fruit in every good work and growing in the knowledge of God,|Keeps walk and fruit metaphors with the repeated growth language.
1:11|being strengthened with every kind of power according to his glorious might, for all endurance and patience, with joy|Retains the piling up of power terms and the purpose of steadfast endurance.
1:12|giving thanks to the Father, who has enabled you to share in the inheritance of the saints in the light.|Preserves divine enablement, inheritance and light imagery.
1:13|He rescued us from the authority of darkness and transferred us into the kingdom of his beloved Son,|Keeps both movements, the authority language and the Son's relational description.
1:14|in whom we have redemption, the forgiveness of sins.|Follows the pinned reading without adding blood and preserves the explanatory apposition.
1:15|He is the image of the invisible God, the firstborn of all creation,|Retains both elevated titles without resolving their theological relation in the verse.

1:16|because in him all things were created—in heaven and on earth, visible and invisible, whether thrones, dominions, rulers or authorities. All things were created through him and for him.|Keeps the cosmic pairs, four powers and threefold relation to creation.
1:17|He is before all things, and in him all things hold together.|Preserves temporal precedence and sustaining cohesion.
1:18|He is the head of the body, the church. He is the beginning, the firstborn from the dead, so that he might be supreme in everything.|Keeps the body image and repeated primacy language.
1:19|For all the fullness was pleased to dwell in him|Preserves the compressed personified wording without supplying an unstated subject.

1:20|and through him to reconcile all things to himself—making peace through the blood of his cross—whether things on earth or things in heaven.|Retains universal reconciliation, violent means and the earth/heaven scope.
1:21|And you, who were once alienated and hostile in mind, as shown by evil deeds—|Keeps prior estrangement and hostility tied to conduct without softening the accusation.
1:22|he has now reconciled in his physical body through death, to present you holy, blameless and beyond accusation before him,|Retains fleshly embodiment, death and all three intended qualities.

1:23|provided that you remain in the faith, firmly founded and steadfast, not shifting away from the hope of the good news you heard, which was proclaimed in all creation under heaven and of which I, Paul, became a minister.|Preserves the condition, building stability and the letter's expansive proclamation claim.

1:24|Now I rejoice in my sufferings for you, and in my flesh I fill up what is lacking in Christ's afflictions for the sake of his body, which is the church.|Keeps the difficult lack-and-filling language and identifies the body without explaining it away.
1:25|I became its minister according to the stewardship God gave me for you, to bring God's word to fullness—|Preserves commissioned stewardship and the ambiguous fullness expression.
1:26|the mystery hidden for ages and generations but now revealed to his saints.|Keeps the long concealment and present disclosure.
1:27|God wanted to make known to them the glorious riches of this mystery among the nations: Christ in you, the hope of glory.|Retains nations, communal indwelling and the appositional hope.

1:28|We proclaim him, warning every person and teaching every person with all wisdom, so that we may present every person mature in Christ.|Preserves the threefold every-person emphasis and both instructional actions.
1:29|For this I labor and struggle, according to his energy powerfully at work in me.|Keeps labor, contest and the repeated working/energy wording.

2:1|I want you to know how great a struggle I have for you, for those in Laodicea and for all who have not seen my face in the flesh,|Preserves the named city and bodily absence alongside the breadth of concern.

2:2|so that their hearts may be encouraged, joined together in love, and reach all the riches of full assurance in understanding: the knowledge of God's mystery, Christ,|Keeps encouragement, love's joining work and Christ as the mystery's apposition.
2:3|in whom all the treasures of wisdom and knowledge are hidden.|Retains treasure and concealment imagery with their comprehensive scope.
2:4|I say this so that no one may deceive you with persuasive speech.|Keeps the warning's purpose and rhetoric's attractive power.

2:5|For though I am absent in the flesh, I am with you in spirit, rejoicing to see your good order and the firmness of your faith in Christ.|Preserves the flesh/spirit contrast and the two disciplined stability images.
2:6|Therefore, just as you received Christ Jesus the Lord, continue to walk in him,|Keeps reception as the basis and the recurring walk metaphor.
2:7|rooted and being built up in him, established in the faith as you were taught, and overflowing with thanksgiving.|Retains the mixed plant/building images and ongoing grammatical aspect.

2:8|Watch out that no one takes you captive through philosophy and empty deception, according to human tradition and the elemental powers of the world, and not according to Christ.|Keeps the captive image, human tradition and the difficult elemental-powers expression.
2:9|For in him all the fullness of deity dwells bodily,|Preserves fullness, deity and bodily dwelling together.
2:10|and you have been filled in him, who is the head of every ruler and authority.|Keeps the shared fullness and supremacy over named powers.

2:11|In him you were also circumcised with a circumcision not performed by hands, in the stripping off of the body of flesh, in Christ's circumcision.|Retains circumcision and bodily stripping images without substituting a doctrinal paraphrase.
2:12|You were buried with him in baptism, in which you were also raised with him through faith in God's power, who raised him from the dead.|Keeps co-burial, co-resurrection and divine agency.

2:13|Though you were dead in your trespasses and the uncircumcision of your flesh, God made you alive together with him, forgiving us all our trespasses.|Preserves death/life reversal and the shift from you to us.
2:14|He erased the written record against us, with its decrees that opposed us. He took it away, nailing it to the cross.|Keeps the documentary image, opposition and crucifixion action.
2:15|He stripped the rulers and authorities and exposed them publicly, triumphing over them in it.|Retains the stripping and triumphal-procession images while leaving the final pronoun open.
2:16|Therefore, do not let anyone judge you about food or drink, or regarding a festival, new moon or Sabbaths.|Preserves the complete calendar and dietary list.
2:17|These are a shadow of what was to come, but the substance belongs to Christ.|Keeps shadow/body contrast while making the bodily metaphor intelligible.

2:18|Do not let anyone disqualify you by delighting in humility and worship of angels, going on about what he has seen, puffed up without cause by his fleshly mind.|Retains the pinned seen reading, judicial image and ironic false humility.

2:19|Such a person does not hold fast to the head, from whom the whole body, supported and held together by joints and ligaments, grows with growth from God.|Keeps anatomical cohesion and emphatic divine growth.
2:20|If you died with Christ to the elemental powers of the world, why, as though still living in the world, do you submit to decrees:|Preserves the conditional death and rhetorical challenge.
2:21|“Do not handle! Do not taste! Do not touch!”|Keeps the terse escalating quoted prohibitions.
2:22|All these things perish as they are used, since they are based on human commands and teachings.|Retains perishability and human origin.

2:23|Such practices have a reputation for wisdom in self-made religion, humility and harsh treatment of the body, but they are of no value against indulgence of the flesh.|Keeps apparent wisdom, bodily severity and the difficult negative assessment.
3:1|Therefore, if you were raised with Christ, seek what is above, where Christ is seated at God's right hand.|Preserves co-resurrection, spatial imagery and enthronement.
3:2|Set your minds on what is above, not on earthly things,|Keeps the sharp directional contrast.
3:3|for you died, and your life is hidden with Christ in God.|Retains the paradox of death and concealed life.
3:4|When Christ, your life, is revealed, then you too will be revealed with him in glory.|Keeps Christ as life and the paired future disclosure.

3:5|So put to death what belongs to your earthly nature: sexual immorality, impurity, passion, evil desire and greed, which is idolatry.|Preserves violent mortification imagery and the full vice list.
3:6|Because of these things God's wrath is coming on the children of disobedience.|Retains the variant-marked clause in the pinned main text and its relational idiom.
3:7|You too once walked in these ways when you lived among them.|Keeps the paired walk/live description of former conduct.
3:8|But now you too must put away all these things: anger, rage, malice, slander and obscene speech from your mouth.|Preserves the clothing-removal image and complete speech-related list.
3:9|Do not lie to one another, since you have stripped off the old self with its practices|Retains mutual scope and the clothing metaphor.
3:10|and put on the new self, which is being renewed in knowledge according to the image of its Creator.|Keeps ongoing renewal, knowledge and restored image.

3:11|Here there is no Greek or Jew, circumcised or uncircumcised, barbarian, Scythian, slave or free; instead, Christ is all and in all.|Preserves every social pair, including slavery, and the climactic Christ claim.

3:12|Therefore, as God's chosen, holy and beloved people, clothe yourselves with heartfelt compassion, kindness, humility, gentleness and patience.|Keeps identity as the basis and the bodily compassion/clothing images.

3:13|Bear with one another and forgive each other if anyone has a complaint against another. Just as the Lord forgave you, so you also must forgive.|Preserves reciprocal endurance, real complaint and the stated pattern.
3:14|Above all these, put on love, which is the bond of maturity.|Keeps clothing and binding images while rendering completeness as maturity.
3:15|Let Christ's peace rule in your hearts, since you were called to this peace in one body. And be thankful.|Retains the umpire-like ruling verb, communal body and terse command.

3:16|Let Christ's word dwell richly among you. Teach and warn one another with all wisdom; with psalms, hymns and spiritual songs, sing to God with gratitude in your hearts.|Keeps mutual teaching, three song forms and interior gratitude.
3:17|Whatever you do, in word or deed, do everything in the name of the Lord Jesus, giving thanks to God the Father through him.|Preserves comprehensive scope and mediated thanksgiving.
3:18|Wives, submit to your husbands, as is fitting in the Lord.|Retains the gender-specific command and its explicit qualification.
3:19|Husbands, love your wives and do not be harsh with them.|Preserves the reciprocal gender-specific command and prohibition of bitterness.
3:20|Children, obey your parents in everything, for this is pleasing in the Lord.|Keeps children, both parents and the comprehensive command.
3:21|Fathers, do not provoke your children, so that they do not become discouraged.|Retains male-specific address and the child's harmful outcome.

3:22|Slaves, obey your earthly masters in everything, not only when they are watching, as people-pleasers, but with sincere hearts, fearing the Lord.|Names slavery and masters directly, retaining surveillance and divided allegiance.
3:23|Whatever you do, work from the heart, as for the Lord and not for people,|Keeps inner-source language and the explicit contrast.
3:24|knowing that from the Lord you will receive the inheritance as your reward. You serve the Lord Christ as a slave.|Retains the inheritance paradox and slave verb directed to Christ.
3:25|For the one who does wrong will be repaid for that wrong, and there is no favoritism.|Keeps accountability and impartiality without restricting the wrongdoer.
4:1|Masters, provide your slaves what is right and fair, knowing that you too have a Master in heaven.|Names both master-slave relations and subjects human masters to another Master.
4:2|Devote yourselves to prayer, staying alert in it with thanksgiving.|Preserves persistence, watchfulness and gratitude.

4:3|At the same time, pray for us too, that God may open a door for the word, so that we may speak Christ's mystery, for which I am in chains.|Keeps the door metaphor, plural request and imprisonment.
4:4|Pray that I may make it clear, as I ought to speak.|Preserves the obligation and clarity sought.
4:5|Walk wisely toward outsiders, making the most of the time.|Keeps social location, walk metaphor and redeemed-opportunity idiom.
4:6|Let your speech always be gracious, seasoned with salt, so that you may know how to answer each person.|Retains the salt image, every occasion and individual response.
4:7|Tychicus, our beloved brother, faithful minister and fellow slave in the Lord, will tell you everything about me.|Preserves the name and all three relational/service titles.
4:8|I am sending him to you for this very reason: that you may know how we are and that he may encourage your hearts.|Keeps the messenger's two purposes and communal encouragement.

4:9|He is coming with Onesimus, our faithful and beloved brother, who is one of you. They will tell you everything happening here.|Names Onesimus and his local belonging without concealing his later slave context.

4:10|Aristarchus, my fellow prisoner, greets you, as does Mark, Barnabas's cousin. You received instructions about him: if he comes to you, welcome him.|Retains all names, kinship and conditional reception instruction.

4:11|Jesus who is called Justus also greets you. These are the only circumcised coworkers for God's kingdom, and they have been a comfort to me.|Keeps the second name, circumcision identity and restricted group claim.

4:12|Epaphras, who is one of you, a slave of Christ Jesus, greets you. He is always struggling for you in his prayers, so that you may stand mature and fully assured in all God's will.|Preserves belonging, slave status, prayer struggle and both desired qualities.
4:13|For I testify that he works hard for you and for those in Laodicea and Hierapolis.|Retains testimony, costly labor and both named neighboring communities.
4:14|Luke, the beloved physician, and Demas greet you.|Keeps both names and Luke's stated occupation.
4:15|Greet the brothers and sisters in Laodicea, as well as Nympha and the church in her house.|Preserves the pinned feminine name and pronoun without harmonizing another tradition.

4:16|After this letter has been read among you, have it read in the church of the Laodiceans too; and you in turn should read the letter from Laodicea.|Keeps reciprocal public reading and both letters without identifying the other letter.
4:17|Tell Archippus, “Pay attention to the ministry you received in the Lord, so that you fulfill it.”|Retains direct address, received service and completion command.
4:18|I, Paul, write this greeting with my own hand. Remember my chains. Grace be with you.|Preserves autograph claim, imprisonment reminder and short plural blessing.
